artworks.title: Chryses Ransoming Chryseis from Agamemnon
artworks.description: Apulian volute-krater (Louvre): Chryses pleads before Agamemnon for Chryseis — the Homeric embassy the king refuses, opening Apollo's plague. Not Chryses son of Minos on Paros.

artworks.title: Chryses Vainly Soliciting the Return of Chryseis
artworks.description: Calvi stages Iliad 1: the priest of Apollo Smintheus before Agamemnon's tent — wreaths, ransom, and the refusal that will empty the Achaean camp.

artworks.title: Chryses Persuading Apollo to Send the Plague
artworks.description: The sequel on the shore: Chryses' prayer answered — Apollo's arrows as the priest's revenge for his daughter's captivity.

artworks.title: Chryses on the Seashore
artworks.description: Preller isolates Homer's old man walking the resounding sea after Agamemnon's threats — the quiet moment before he calls Apollo.

artworks.title: Chryses Begs Agamemnon for His Daughter
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum engraving from the Speculum Heroicum: Chryses' supplication as a stock Homeric emblem — the priest who starts the wrath.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book 1 opens on Chryses: Agamemnon refuses his ransom, Apollo sends the plague, and the priest's prayer becomes the first wound of the poem.

popCulture.title: Chryses (priest of Apollo)
popCulture.description: Priest of Apollo at Chryse, father of Chryseis — not Chryses son of Minos slain by Heracles on Paros.
